speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, whatever changes there may be in the socio-economic environment, one thing we cannot escape from is the psychological motivation for a person to seek a job and be gainfully employed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, the availability of jobs, good paying jobs, matters for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But it is not uncommon to hear accounts about how Singaporeans have been discriminated by errant employers, company owners and human resource (HR) managers who exploit our system unfairly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The matter on fair employment practices has always been close to my heart.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have raised this issue in my maiden speech here four years ago and I am grateful for the opportunity to file this Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is because I strongly believe in the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices' (TAFEP's) potential to tackle discriminatory employment and hiring practices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many Members of this House have spoken on TAFEP-related issues over the years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They highlighted how instilling fair and progressive employment practices among employers remains a critical goal of TAFEP.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But that goal is a work in progress.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The aim of this Motion is to suggest how to strengthen TAFEP to achieve its goal.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the purposes of filing this Motion, I want to focus on just two main issues.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, age discrimination; and second, efforts to localise jobs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, looking at the labour data, the employment rate of older workers has shown steady gains over time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is a good testament to efforts to allow our older workers to continue contributing to our economy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That sets the macro context on this issue.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Things are improving but this demographic segment could be susceptible and needs to be monitored over time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The retirement and re-employment ages have also been raised over the years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is to keep pace with our ageing population.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It encourages older Singaporeans to stay socially, physically and mentally active, make good use of their skills and experience.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Unfortunately, some employers are not keeping pace with the times.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This may be anecdotal, but, I have met Singaporeans in their 60s, 50s and 40s even, who have trouble seeking employment for more than a year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They have the qualifications, even went for courses and networking sessions, took career coaches' advice and brushed up their resume, interviewing skills and so on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are prepared to take pay cuts and explore other industries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I know there are companies that employ or are willing to employ seniors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But we need more employers to do this.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One resident told me he was advised by a career coach, after numerous job applications that met with no responses, that he should shorten his work history so as not to emphasise his real age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Recently, I sat in at a professional image coaching session.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Most had recently been retrenched, in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The coach had dedicated an entire section on sprucing up one's image to look youthful on social media.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even WhatsApp's profile pictures had to be carefully curated to make them look younger than their actual age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Possible penalties range from curtailment of work pass privileges to employers paying compensation for any wrongful dismissal.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have heard some feedback that current penalties as too lenient, lack of bite.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, international studies have shown that the effects of such anti-discrimination legislation on employment outcomes are not conclusive.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the United States, studies showed that age discrimination against seniors remain prevalent, even with the Federal Age Discrimination in Employment Act and similar state laws in place.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In particular, legislation can potentially deter hiring, especially when they result in higher termination costs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, in short, anti-discrimination legislation may not be the solution to encourage greater hiring of those in their 50s and above.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are other non-legislation efforts undertaken abroad that we could explore or take note of.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Two countries have gone beyond the usual provision of upskilling courses and interview workshops to motivate the unemployed and encourage hiring of seniors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Belgium, the campaign "There is no age for talent" was launched in 2017 and it included events organised by unemployed people aged 55 and above, to motivate their peers and employers to address ageist attitudes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The "Active Together 45+" programme was started in a city in Poland to help 120 socially excluded persons to return to the labour market.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, the message to get out to all employers is that: capabilities matter more and not age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are also urged to age-audit their workforce and make the data publicly available.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Singapore, we set numerous targets to achieve progress, for issues ranging from carbon emissions to smoking rate.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can we introduce one for increasing the older workforce so companies should set targets for older worker proportion of the workforce?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With our steadily greying population, it is only a matter of time that this becomes inevitable.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Employers should embrace it, instead of avoiding it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, the onus is on the companies to set this with unions, as the needs of the firms may significantly depend on the industry and the nature of work.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second suggestion: certification schemes are part of the push to eradicate ageism in other countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One example is the Austrian NESTORGOLD programme that also supports companies in developing age-inclusive and diverse work environments.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Singapore, companies that wish to signal their intention to be a fair employer sign the Employers' Pledge of Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This certification can be a criterion for the application of various grants and support.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Disruptive changes in the economy and economic cycles have made it even more challenging for the older unemployed to find work.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One can sink into depression, especially if they have done all they could, including attending courses to upskill themselves, but are seeing little progress for their efforts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, I move on to efforts to localise jobs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Singapore's context of a small open economy, competitiveness and growth are important.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore needs the skills of foreign specialists to supplement our workforce in areas where we are lacking in expertise.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, we cannot continue to have inflow of foreign specialists in perpetuity without regard for the well-being of our Singapore Core.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the other hand, we also want to help our companies succeed with the right talent, but we want Singaporeans to participate in their success.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Indeed, during one of our Committee of Supply debates in 2016, Members spoke about building the Singaporean Core.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Then-Minister Lim Swee Say acknowledged the perception among some Singaporeans who felt they were in a minority in their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This was largely because of companies that allowed pockets of foreigners to concentrate and failed to work on building the Singaporean Core.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MOM has various policies in place to encourage companies to hire Singaporeans, such as the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF).

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But I feel TAFEP need not be too shy to name companies that have not acted in good faith.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Partly, it will send a stronger signal and may trigger whistleblowers who can provide leads to check up other companies so it is harder for them to get away.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Sometimes, all it takes is some clever drafting of job applications to ensure that the job goes to the preferred candidate.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is why I feel we can enhance our best practices further to ensure a good balance in the economy and improve local-foreign workforce complementarity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have some suggestions to enhance our tools and mechanisms where possible to help address some of the issues I raised above.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As I try to come up with these suggestions, I have this at the back of my mind.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I meet corporates, small and medium enterprises in Singapore and regionally as part of my work, and labour force issues like talent and cost are always a key factor.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We take it for granted as workers sometimes assume companies will always want to be in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This depends on whether Singapore remains attractive as a place for business and to continue to create jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the other hand, as a Member of Parliament, I see residents coming to see me, giving feedback about the difficulties in getting a job.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I just met a resident trained in information technology who is around 50 years old and recently lost his job and currently unsuccessfully looking for a job for the past six to 12 months.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: He has a special needs child and has a family to support, so his concerns are real.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, individuals matter, and individuals' difficulties matter, too.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have the opportunity to see these two sides of the coin on this issue.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A concern, of course, is irresponsible businesses taking full advantage of the business argument always.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have been thinking what else can be done to improve things where possible in Singapore's context without tipping the balance negatively for the economy and Singapore's competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My first suggestion: we must take action against companies, if no attempt is made to localise workforce over a period of time as this is not reflective of good corporate citizenship.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: By "localisation targets" I mean, proportion of workforce that is local or setting a target for overall local proportion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It needs to be set by the companies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This can be targeted for a range of skills and may need to be company-specific or dependent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It could, for example, incorporate elements of training for eventual local employment, with a specific localisation target in three to five years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This, I feel, would make TAFEP wield a bigger stick in a targeted sustainable manner, working with employers, to provision for opportunities for our workers whilst at the same time making business sense.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second suggestion: but it cannot be all sticks, there could be some carrots.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It also provides for firms to send locals abroad for training to improve local-foreign workforce complementarity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The funding support for CTP can include salary and training support for foreign and local specialists, as well as Singaporean trainees on overseas attachments to acquire new capabilities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But the current CTP, as it stands, applies to incoming foreign specialists.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At this wage level, many Singaporeans should be given the jobs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope, Mr Deputy Speaker, MOM and TAFEP would support these suggestions to enhance TAFEP's carrots and stick.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And sometimes, it is natural for employers to place the perceived interests of their company over the perceived interests of another individual or the worker, even if they acknowledge that this individual is from a more vulnerable group.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, left on its own, discrimination in the labour landscape is not something that will diminish over time by itself.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Yet, its costs are too great to not address and to not address now.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I agree with the Member Mr Saktiandi Supaat that age discrimination or ageism is an issue we have to watch closely.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It should have no place in an ageing workforce like ours but, unfortunately, it exists and makes our society less inclusive than it should be.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, like he also rightly pointed out, there are no silver bullet solutions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Based on my ground experience in the Labour Movement, age discrimination can take two forms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, the intentional variant, employers hire younger workers at the expense of older workers even though they could be equal or even surpass the younger workers in capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These employers can be quite artful in rejecting candidates at the pre-hiring stage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: When already in employment, they might let go of workers through undeserved performance mark-downs; or making work assignments unduly difficult; or to offer workers a "rock or a hard place" job option at re-employment as a subtle way of signalling "perhaps, you should go".

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These are the egregious cases where the errant employers must be taken to task.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, preferring younger workers presumably because they have fewer medical problems or a longer career runway.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Or allowing unkind age-related remarks to go unaddressed at workplaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Or some advertisements that are discriminatory without intending to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, there are some advertisements seeking to hire digital natives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: That would clearly exclude me, in my 40s, because I was born in the age of mainframes and typewriters in the 1970s.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While I am not a digital native, I can pick up the digital skills to be a digital migrant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Both of these variants clearly require quite different approaches.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Before we discuss the possible approaches, we must note two issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is good progress and we must persist in this effort.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, interventions should not result in undue deadweight compliance costs without overriding benefits to the older workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, many pieces of legislation introduced overseas have not resulted in tangible benefits.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The question is how do we protect workers from age discrimination without unintentionally making them less attractive to hire?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How does Singapore continue to be pro-business and pro-worker at the same time?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I understand the intent of the Fair Consideration Framework is to improve HR practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But there could be alternatives to finetune the process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, the Singapore Police Force publishes the three-year grading for the security agencies annually.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The security agencies would, therefore, work very hard to improve their processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Perhaps MOM can publish the egregious ones and publicly track them for a certain period of time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Companies must also know that while we offer second chances, we will also not hesitate to take tougher measures if you are recalcitrant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: To paraphrase Lord Hewart CJ, "justice must be done and seen to be done." Our workers must know that we have been standing up for them and justice will be brought to bear on bad employers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And if you have improved, it would also be reflected transparently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In fact, evidence are largely based on circumstantial observations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, if a company lets go of an older worker and subsequently hires a younger one subsequently three to six months down the road, it is difficult to prove a case of ageism.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But that is with a longitudinal analysis of a company's practices that can surface discriminatory hiring or employment practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I think these studies will also show up companies that had consistently favoured foreign workers over local talent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Labour Movement will certainly be keen to support such a study.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Third, we need to correct the unintended ageism at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many employers hire younger workers simply because they are cheaper, or have higher learning abilities or a longer runway.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Learning ability is as much a capability as a skill that is honed over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And there is no runway to speak of if your younger worker who tends to change job every two to three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We cannot legislate away the myths, but we can educate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And that is where the tripartism way of improving capabilities of our HR professionals is paramount.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Our goal in building the Singapore workforce is clear – one that is inclusive and built upon a strong Singaporean Core.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Confronting ageism and building a strong Singaporean Core must be the aim of all companies and agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It need not always be the stick, like Member Mr Saktiandi Supaat has said.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must also reward companies for being aligned to the national mission.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I encourage the Government to continue to maintain this signal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I also agree with Member Saktiandi Supaat that inclusive and exemplary companies should be rewarded in access to grants and support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The difficulties in building an inclusive workforce with a strong Singaporean Core have multiplied because of rapid economic changes and our ageing workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: No one will doubt that professional team sports are one of the most ruthlessly competitive industries in the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to thank Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Desmond Choo for speaking about this important issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our overarching goal is to develop fair and progressive employment practices within the backdrop of harmonious labour relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In labour-constrained Singapore, where we continue to create a surplus of jobs, businesses have a natural incentive to improve their employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, as the Members noted, some employers may still lag behind with outdated practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But let me beclear: workplace discrimination, even in small pockets, is simply not acceptable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must do everything we can to stamp it out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To this end, MOM and our tripartite partners adopt a multi-pronged approach that actively promotes fair and progressive workplaces, stay vigilant to detect and investigate all forms of workplace discrimination, and acts firmly against errant employers while helping them improve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It recognises that workplace practices are shaped not by Government only and certainly not through legislation alone, as Mr Sakitiandi Supaat acknowledged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Employers and unions all play a critical part.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our measures include the tripartite standards, the Human Capital Partnerships Programme and the Tripartite Alliance Awards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These publicly recognise companies with fair, responsible and progressive employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat suggested certifying age inclusive companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Tripartite Standards on Age-friendly Workplace Practices already does so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This includes not using age as a selection criterion for recruitment, and designing jobs and workplaces to be age-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: TAFEP is a tripartite body that (a) educates employers and workers on the merits of inclusive and progressive practices; (b) issues tripartite guidelines on fair employment practices; and (c) investigate reports of workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They state that employers should recruit and select employees on the basis of merit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To be clear, hiring a younger worker, in itself, may not reflect discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The key is to consider employees based on merit without discriminating on any measure, including age, race, gender, religion, marital status, family responsibilities or disability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A younger worker should also be given a chance to prove his merit even if he has less experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But, more importantly, employers must also give fair consideration to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When TAFEP finds employers that fail to abide by the guidelines, it works with MOM to take enforcement action, including curtailing work pass privileges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our investigations found that it had rejected 20% of job applications for no reason other than age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Desmond Choo will be pleased to know that this company had their work pass privileges curtailed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They certainly did not think that TAFEP or MOM were lenient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For six months, they had to deal with unhappy customers and potential liquidated damages for project delays.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM and TAFEP also take stern action through FCF, which requires employers to fairly consider all jobseekers, in particular, Singaporeans should not be discriminated against.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under FCF, employers must advertise on a national Jobsbank before submitting Employment Pass (EP) applications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is to ensure that these job openings are made public and not only to a close circle of friends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Employers that treat these advertisements as paper exercise or what some say, "wayang" have been uncovered and have been taken to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, MOM and TAFEP have been improving the methods to detect and scrutinise suspicious employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, TAFEP investigated a metal fabrication firm that applied for an EP for an engineer role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The employer required candidates to have a Bachelors Degree in Mechanical Engineering but this was not stated in the Jobsbank posting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The employer also disregarded a local candidate who had a Masters Degree in Mechanical and Materials Engineering and provided false information to TAFEP by claiming to have interviewed three other candidates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, they had pre-selected the foreigner and did not interview anyone else.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM rejected the EP application and debarred the employer from hiring new foreign workers for six months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM also proactively identifies firms with workforce profiles that suggest possible discrimination against Singaporeans, such as having an exceptional share of foreign professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs), compared to the industry peers or an extremely high concentration of a single foreign nationality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We place such employers on the FCF watchlist and scrutinise their EP applications closely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While MOM clamps down on the EP applications, TAFEP also engages the employers on a one-on-one basis to help them improve their HR practices and support local hiring.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Of the 600 firms, TAFEP has helped 260 firms to improve and exit the watchlist so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also deal firmly with those who try to play games with us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, we have employers on the watchlist who used related entities to apply for EPs to by-pass our controls.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For such cases, we curtail the work pass privilege of all their related entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sakitiandi Supaat called for the EP policy to be tightened.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister of State, you have three more minutes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And experienced EP holders in their mid-40s would need to earn much more to qualify, compared to a similarly experienced local PMET.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, our last EP salary requirement was adjusted in 2017.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As part of our regular process, we will review if it needs to be updated to preserve a level playing field for local PMETs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Despite the employer tactics that Mr Desmond Choo described, older worker employment has gone up steadily.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The unemployment rate for workers aged 50 and above has also been consistently lower than the overall unemployment rate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The FCF watchlist has also raised awareness and shifted employer behaviour.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, locals continue to hold the majority of jobs that companies can hire EPs for.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I should also add that our strong stance against favouring foreigners has not gone unnoticed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: From the view of business leaders, they see far more favourable regimes outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If leading global companies think twice about investing in Singapore or rethink their future plans for Singapore, the result could be fewer good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But ultimately, we must also continue to create good jobs and help more Singaporeans access them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also spoke about capability transfer and called for businesses to step up in localising their workforce to support Singapore's competitiveness and workforce sustainability.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will study Mr Saktiandi Supaat's suggestion to expand the CTP and including how it can support companies to set localisation targets.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To conclude, workplace discrimination of any kind is unacceptable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In Singapore, the tripartite partners are fully committed to stamping out workplace discrimination altogether.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We welcome and look forward to more initiatives in the Labour Movement to tackle workplace discrimination of all forms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And as Member Desmond Choo mentioned earlier, every worker matters.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Let us also ensure that Singapore remains competitive and redouble our efforts to help more locals access the jobs that are created.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.
